<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-api-reference.ts from sdk/openapi.json. Do not edit — including in Studio; the next build replaces this file. -->

::api-operation{method="GET" path="/v1/report_dashboards/{id}/reports"}
#docs
The query options are DEFAULTS — they fill in only what a tile did not pin, so a tile's own choice always wins. An org-level dashboard REQUIRES `business`; a business-scoped one REFUSES a `business` naming a different one rather than ignoring it. One tile failing never fails the dashboard: that tile carries `error` and the rest still resolve.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | **yes** | The report dashboard's id. |

## Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `business` | `string` | no | Required for an org-level dashboard, which has no business of its own. |
| `range` | `string` | no | The period to report on. |
| `currency` | `string` | no | The currency to show amounts in (ISO-4217 code). |
| `granularity` | `string` | no | How the period is split into buckets. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Success |
| `400` | Missing business for an org-level dashboard, or a mismatched business |
| `404` | No such dashboard, or not visible to you |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/report_dashboards/dash_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/reports" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY"
```

#response

```json [200 OK]
{}
```

```json [400 Bad Request]
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
```
